clue.text: Italian unable to see in the shade

parts.note: a Venetian is an Italian from Venice
someone unable to see is blind

explanation.surface: A sightless Italian sits out of the sun in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A slatted window blind is a kind of shade that keeps out sunlight.

clue.text: Personal stake in undertaking strangely, it's never tested

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of these words come out in an odd, rearranged order

explanation.surface: Someone backing an untried venture has money riding on something nobody has tried out.
explanation.definitionFit: A vested interest is a personal stake, often financial, held in some enterprise or outcome.

clue.text: Someone giving information about one racket

indicators.note: about means the informer word goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A grass talks about a single fraudulent scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like a criminal scheme to go with the informer, but it means a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, which is simply noise.

clue.text: Assume midshipman is to rest

parts.note: to take it is to assume, as in 'I take it you agree'
Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel of that name

explanation.surface: A naval officer is presumed to be off duty.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Midshipman Easy is an 1836 novel by Frederick Marryat, so 'midshipman' stands for EASY.
explanation.definitionFit: To take it easy is an idiom for resting or relaxing.

clue.text: In contact with military commander, in a way

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone is in touch with an army chief, after a fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaning against a wall means being in physical contact with it, so the preposition fits.

clue.text: Encourages county towards the north

parts.note: Bucks is the short name of Buckinghamshire, an English county
up means northwards, as on a map

explanation.surface: A shire heading north lifts everyone's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is Buckinghamshire, a county just north-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To buck someone up is a British idiom for cheering or encouraging them.

clue.text: Incomplete graphic, one that's found on computer screen

definitions.text: one that's found on computer screen

indicators.note: incomplete says the word for graphic loses its ending

parts.note: iconic means pictorial or graphic, relating to images

explanation.surface: An unfinished picture is displayed on a monitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A small symbol clicked on a computer desktop is called an icon.

clue.text: Embroider a table cloth, and beat it

parts.note: to do embroidery is to embroider, so 'do' stands for it
a runner is a long narrow cloth laid along a table

explanation.surface: Someone does needlework on a tablecloth and then wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat it' seems to finish the needlework story, but it is slang for running away.
explanation.definitionFit: To do a runner is British slang for leaving in a hurry, especially without paying, as 'beat it' means to clear off.

clue.text: Is it safe to criticise arrest? One's at your throat

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
to pan a play is to criticise it harshly
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A nervous critic wonders whether it is safe to attack a police seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At your throat' sounds like an attacker, but it is just where the collar sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A Peter Pan collar is a flat, round-cornered collar that lies around the neck.

clue.text: Fuss resulting when sweaters are back to front

indicators.note: back to front means the word for sweaters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: knits are knitted garments such as sweaters

explanation.surface: There is an uproar when jumpers are put on the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick up a stink is to make a fuss, so the noun means a row or commotion.

clue.text: Roads in American city

definitions.meaning: roads, or a roadstead, is sheltered water where ships ride at anchor
a city in Alaska, the largest in the state

explanation.definitionFit: An anchorage is a place for ships to anchor, like roads; it is also the Alaskan city's name.

clue.text: Tree: it's seen flourishing all round -by me?

indicators.note: all round says the shuffled letters go around the tree word, enclosing it
flourishing, waved about, says these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the yew is an evergreen tree

explanation.surface: A tree is admired as it blooms on every side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourishing' makes EITNESS from IT'S SEEN, and 'all round' puts it around YEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who saw something happen can say it was seen by them, which is what a witness on the spot is.

clue.text: Fibre-producing plant that overran SE England

definitions.meaning: a plant whose coarse fibre makes sacking and twine
a member of the Germanic people who settled Kent in the fifth century

explanation.definitionFit: Jute is the fibre plant; a Jute was one of the tribe that invaded and settled Kent.

clue.text: Handle being hag-ridden

parts.note: hag-ridden normally means tormented, but here it is a long handle a witch literally rides on

explanation.definitionFit: A witch, or hag, traditionally rides a broom, so its long handle is what she rides.

clue.text: Most silly birds may be found here

definitions.meaning: the superlative of a word meaning foolish or pointless
read as three words, a place where birds sit

explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly, so inanest is the silliest; split up it reads 'in a nest'.

clue.text: At bar, ale's changed for mineral

indicators.note: changed says these letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: In the pub, someone's beer has been swapped for a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mineral' looks like a mineral water in the pub, but it means the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft white mineral, a form of gypsum used for carving.

clue.text: Bargain on the regular amount for vegetable

indicators.note: on means the bargain word is placed after, attached to, the other piece

parts.note: par is the normal or standard amount
a snip is a bargain, something cheap

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a cheap deal on the usual quantity of greens.
explanation.definitionFit: The parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Stern matrons relaxed

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Severe hospital matrons finally unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' looks like an adjective for the matrons, but it is the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A transom is a crosspiece forming the flat stern of a boat, so it stands for the stern.

clue.text: Preserve parent in condition? On the contrary

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the condition goes inside the parent, not the parent inside the condition

parts.note: mummy is a word for a mother, a parent
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A carer wonders whether to keep a parent in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'parent in condition' would put the parent inside; 'On the contrary' flips which piece holds the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To mummify is to preserve a body by embalming and drying it.

clue.text: Poke gold right inside cover

indicators.note: inside says these pieces go within the cover word

parts.note: to span is to cover or extend across
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone prods gold, putting it right under a lid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poke' looks like a verb, but it is an old word for a bag or pouch, as in 'a pig in a poke'. A sporran is the pouch worn with a Scottish kilt.
explanation.definitionFit: A poke is a small bag or pouch, and a sporran is the pouch worn at the front of a kilt.

clue.text: Unusual setting for garnets

indicators.note: setting means arranging, as a jeweller sets stones, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes an odd mount for some red gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and unusual are synonyms for out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Bus, having dropped us off, leaves wide thoroughfare

indicators.note: leaves means the remaining letter goes away from the word for wide

parts.note: broad means wide

indicators.note: having dropped says the bus word loses some letters
off completes the dropping, the letters taken off the bus word

parts.note: the clue word is used as written
the word us is taken as written

explanation.surface: A bus drops passengers off, then pulls away from a broad street.
explanation.walkthrough: BUS minus US leaves B, and taking B from BROAD leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A road is a thoroughfare, a public way for traffic.

clue.text: As president visiting a former capital, I am first of all a showman

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am, and 'first of all' says it leads the answer
pres is the abbreviation for president, who is here on a visit next to what follows
Rio de Janeiro was Brazil's capital until 1960

explanation.surface: A head of state on a trip to an old capital boasts of being a great entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces out of order; 'first of all' tells you the I AM piece leads. Rio de Janeiro was replaced as Brazil's capital by Brasilia in 1960.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and promotes shows, so he is a showman.

clue.text: Grow older in state prison

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
the pen, short for penitentiary, is prison

explanation.surface: An inmate ages behind bars in a state jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit and cheese ripen as they age and mature, so ripen means grow older.

clue.text: Open up! It's'the Prince

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for open is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ajar means slightly open, of a door

explanation.surface: Someone bangs on the door demanding entry for royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja is an Indian king or prince.

clue.text: Surrounded by endless hubbub, I'll get tense reversing into spot

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed: 'Surrounded by endless hubbub, I'll get tense reversing into spot'; TAUT reversed gives TUAT, but no word for hubbub shortened gives the remaining S...ION around it, so the parse cannot be completed honestly.
annotationWithheld.clue: Surrounded by endless hubbub, I'll get tense reversing into spot

clue.text: Drive from member ending up in bad lie

indicators.note: ending up in means finishing inside, so the member is placed within the other letters
bad signals that the letters of lie are spoiled, put in a different order

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is shifted from an awkward spot on the golf course.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is golf: a 'bad lie' is an awkward ball position, and 'bad' is the anagram signal turning the lie into IEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push forward.

clue.text: A whiz at mental arithmetic, I've done your sums for you

definitions.meaning: literally a person who is quick, or ready, at reckoning figures

definitions.text: I've done your sums for you
definitions.meaning: the voice of a book of printed tables giving ready-made calculations

explanation.definitionFit: A ready reckoner is a booklet of precomputed tables; read literally it is someone quick at calculation.
